mechanism: fixed viewBox coordinate system; rig.json declares slots with envelopes+anchors+layer order; each slot holds interchangeable SVG parts; render-and-compare against reference; sampled-combination verification
inputs: reference image or character brief + variant counts
outputs: SVG avatar + swappable parts folder + preview sheets + picker page
parts_model: slots with envelopes/anchors; parts overlap neighbours >=8 units; palette variables only
tooling: python + playwright(chromium) + pillow/numpy/scipy; scripts in approach folder
notes: THE built approach: 10 slots, 25 parts, selftest-proven verifier. Full method in approaches/modular-svg-rig/README.md. Re-run selftest before trusting after any folder move.

mechanism: name -> initials (1-3 glyphs) rendered on a deterministic background (color from hash of name); pure SVG/HTML/CSS
parts_model: no parts model - the name IS the input; variants = palette/shape schemes
tooling: None required (any renderer; even server-side string templating)
notes: Cheapest fallback that always works offline; watch initials collapse for CJK/non-latin names - define the grapheme rule explicitly.

mechanism: arbitrary string -> deterministic symmetric grid pattern (GitHub-style); identicon shape set drawn from hash bits
parts_model: cells/shapes are procedural - swapping = different seed
tooling: none required; pure function of the seed
notes: Zero-collision visual identity, no reference image possible; not humanizing - users do not recognize themselves in it.

mechanism: style + query-parameter URL drives a deterministic avatar generator server-side (dicebear-class); parts map 1:1 to URL params
parts_model: parts = URL components (each param swappable); consistency guaranteed by the generator
tooling: HTTP client; verify current param docs - these APIs change
notes: Fastest mix-and-match without owning a rig; tradeoff: external dependency + style ceiling. Cross-ref: fahlwy data.csv category=avatar lists working endpoints.

mechanism: pick/stack emoji glyphs (face + accessories) composed in a frame; user-chosen or rule-mapped
parts_model: parts = layered emoji glyphs; z-order and baseline alignment are the failure points
tooling: any text-rendering stack; font differences across platforms are a real leak
notes: Playful, zero drawing skill needed; platform emoji-font variance means the same avatar renders differently - ship as raster or embedded-glyph SVG.

mechanism: user photo cropped to frame (circle/squircle), optionally face-detected for centering, stylized or left real
parts_model: no parts; variants = crop mask / stylization level
tooling: face-detect or center-weighted crop; image tooling of choice
notes: Highest recognition, lowest privacy; processing happens on the real person's biometric - state storage/retention before shipping; RTL/rotation EXIF traps.

mechanism: text-to-image model prompted with a character spec; seed fixed for reproducibility
parts_model: no true parts model - restyling a single feature means regenerating the whole image
tooling: imagegen tool available in the environment
notes: Infinite styles, no swappability and no palette consistency across regenerations; fine for one-off hero avatars, wrong for a family of matching ones.

mechanism: one hand-drawn SVG for one avatar - no rig, no slots
parts_model: none - if a second variant is requested, promote to modular-svg-rig instead
tooling: any vector tool or direct XML writing
notes: The honest answer when the user wants ONE avatar and no swapping; do not build a rig nobody asked for.
